about: Trigger eval queries for this skill's description. A query is labelled with whether the skill should activate for it; the negatives are near-misses that share vocabulary with the skill but need something else. Split fixed so successive description edits are compared on the same ground: tune against train, judge against validation. One validation label was corrected by hand (issues #25, #24): `why is this endpoint slow in production` is a negative here, not a positive. `make eval` on `dab7767` ran it three times as a realistic turn and Page fired 0x on every one, and the body says why -- Phase 1 reviews `the change, not the codebase` and needs a `git diff`, Phase 4's performance list is a review checklist applied to that diff, and the phase stops outright when no `__REVIEW_VERDICT__` arrived. A live latency regression supplies none of those, so complying means diagnosing a running system, which is not what this skill does. Its nine other positives are all review-of-a-change; this was the only diagnostic one, and the set already drew the same line with `fix the slow query`. That asserted negative was spent to restore the positive, because the relabelled query now draws the line with three measured runs behind it. This corrects what #24 and #25 both claim -- they read the 0/3 as a description gap.
how_to_run: `make eval` is the committed runner, but it covers only the queries a 3-sample blind-router baseline actually missed, not this whole file -- see CLAUDE.md for why 13 and not 380. To judge the rest: `skillgrade` runs a labelled set like this one and exits non-zero when the pass rate falls below a threshold. Needing nothing installed: run each query with `claude -p --output-format json` and count the runs whose transcript contains a Skill tool_use naming this skill. Cheapest of all, and closest to the router's real conditions: give a model only the name and description of every installed skill, with no bodies and no repo access, and have it pick one skill or none per query. `claude plugin eval`, which `make eval` drives, is generally available rather than early access; what it needs instead is a credential, a network and real money -- $0.142 a run, measured -- which is why it sits outside `make test` and CI does not run it. It will not reproduce this file query-for-query either: a bare query does not fire a skill, so a case is one of these queries rewritten as a realistic turn. This file stays the cheap, free, offline record.
